_why: Written 2026-08-11 when the Gemburrow subsite was first folded into this origin. Gemburrow's privacy story is strong but NOT absolute: the game makes exactly one kind of network call — a Daily Dig score posted to Supabase — and every claim below is worded to leave room for it. Verified against /Users/dee/Developer/DrVanus/gemburrow at commit a6d2fd4.

evidence: There is no sign-in surface anywhere: a case-insensitive grep of gemburrow/game.js for signin, sign_in, login, password, email, oauth, 'apple id', GameCenter and GameKit returns nothing. The game is one file, so that grep covers the whole client.

SCOPE: the Daily Dig leaderboard identifies a device, not a person. game.js Meta.mint() generates a random UUID on first run and derives the display name 'MOLE-' + its first four characters (game.js:690-696); the player cannot choose or edit it. privacy.html gives that identifier its own section and says plainly that it is not an Apple ID, not an advertising identifier, and not linked to any identity. Do not reword the site's 'no account' into 'nothing identifies you'.

No analytics, attribution or crash SDK is linked. package.json dependencies are exactly @capacitor/android, @capacitor/cli, @capacitor/core, @capacitor/haptics, @capacitor/ios and @capacitor/preferences — no Firebase, no Sentry, no AppsFlyer, no GA.

The only outbound HTTP in the client is the leaderboard: game.js:750 (POST a daily score) and game.js:769 (GET the day's top rows). The other two fetch() calls (game.js:939, 942) load the game's own bundled audio from the app package. No behavioural, session or crash telemetry exists to send.

native/ios/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy declares NSPrivacyTracking = false and requests no advertising identifier; tools/apply_ios_overlay.py stamps it into the Xcode project on every ship and step 4 of ship_ios.sh asserts it against the built binary.

No advertising SDK is linked into the build (package.json dependency list above), and a grep of game.js for admob, adsbygoogle and revenuecat returns nothing. There is no ad unit, no placement and no rewarded path.

SCOPE: this is a plain, present-tense claim about the shipping build, not a promise about every future version. If an ad SDK is ever integrated, this approval and the site's 'No ads' card both expire.

The save (localStorage key gb_meta_v1, mirrored to Capacitor Preferences) holds only game state: hoardTotal, tutorialDone, bestDaily, bestFree, coins, owned, equipped, careerLevel, careerStars, plus the random clientId and the derived MOLE- name (game.js:675-677 and the careerStars/careerLevel writes at game.js:1732-1750). privacy.html enumerates exactly that list.

No field anywhere collects a name, email, address, phone number or contact detail: there is no text-entry surface in the game at all, and the leaderboard name is generated rather than typed, which is why a personal detail cannot reach the public board.
The game requests no location, contacts, photos, microphone or camera permission — no such usage-description key exists in the Info.plist stamped by tools/apply_ios_overlay.py.

no_purchases._RETRACTED: 2026-08-22. This approval is DEAD and must not be relied on again. gemburrow.full.unlock shipped that day — a non-consumable declared in gemburrow/store/iap-catalog.json and read by game.js (var FULL_PRODUCT, the Ent journal, careerCap()), with native/ios/GemburrowStore.swift as its StoreKit 2 handler. The 2026-08-11 evidence below was true when written and is kept only so the next reader can see WHY the grep passed: it greps a build that no longer exists.
evidence: STALE (2026-08-11): There is no StoreKit dependency and no purchase code: a case-insensitive grep of game.js for storekit, purchase, iap and revenuecat returns only two comment lines about 'purchased cosmetic ids' and 'a purchased deeper pick' — both referring to spending in-game coins (game.js:672, 1195).

STILL TRUE: The shop's six dig walls and the Deeper Pick (250 coins) are bought with COINS, and coins are only ever earned by digging — store/iap-catalog.json _MODEL: 'Coins are earned by digging and are not for sale — that is a design law, not an omission.' Wall prices were re-priced to 22,000c for all six on 2026-08-21, so do not quote the 0..2400 figures this entry used to carry.

EXACTLY ONE product exists and it is a non-consumable: store/iap-catalog.json products[] holds a single entry, id gemburrow.full.unlock, display_name 'The Full Burrow'. _MODEL: 'no subscription, no consumable, no currency pack, and no ads.' The site may say 'one optional purchase' and must not say 'no in-app purchases', 'nothing to buy' or 'no purchase path'.

WHAT IT UNLOCKS, and what stays free: _BOUNDARY.unlocked_by_purchase is career levels 11-40 and the 14-day daily archive; _BOUNDARY.free_forever is Free Dig, the Daily Dig with its leaderboard and 14-day league, career levels 1-10, all 27 contracts, and the whole shop and wardrobe. game.js FREE_CAREER_LEVELS = 10 and CAREER_MAX = 40 agree.

CONTENT, NEVER POWER — this is what lets the site keep its fairness card. iap-catalog _NEVER_SELLABLE: 'Nothing purchasable may touch the SIM — not swings, not satchel slots, not jar content, not the restock valve... The gate is CONTENT (which levels you may enter), never power.' game.js says the same at careerCap(): 'How far up the ladder this save may go. The ONLY thing the entitlement changes anywhere in the game.' tools/probe_iap_fairness.js proves the daily is byte-identical for a fresh save and an owns-everything save.

NO PRICE ON THIS SITE, AND NONE IN THIS FILE. iap-catalog.json flags its own planned_price_usd with _price_is_a_hint: 'planned_price_usd is a console-setup crib and NOTHING else. The paywall renders the storefront's own localized displayPrice; hardcoding a dollar figure is an App Review 3.1.2 rejection on every non-USD storefront.' The number is also unshipped — console_steps_for_vanus is still open and _PLATFORM_STATE_2026_08_22 records iOS as 'SELLABLE once the console work is done' — so no storefront has ever charged it. A US dollar figure was written into index.html's FAQ answer and its JSON-LD twin and was removed on 2026-08-24; this contract dropped it in the same pass, because a public file under /gemburrow/ publishes whatever it quotes. The approved claim is WHAT the unlock opens, never what it costs.

SCOPE — THE BROWSER BUILD HAS NO STORE AT ALL. The deployed play/game.js contains no careerCap, no Store, no GemburrowStore and no paywall (grep, 2026-08-24), and CAREER_MAX is 40 there, so the whole ladder is open in a browser. iap-catalog _NO_STORE_NO_WALL says the same of any storeless build. Claims about the browser build must be scoped with 'in your browser'; index.html's hero note is.

TRUE HALF: nothing recharges on a clock. There is no energy, stamina or lives system anywhere in game.js, and the archive was opened precisely because 'a daily playable only on its own day is an APPOINTMENT WINDOW, which the design forbids in the same breath as energy and lives' (game.js, THE ARCHIVE note).

FALSE HALF, TWICE CAUGHT: 'No timers' is a forbidden string. CFG.timedDur is 45 and SLOT_CLS is ['easy','med','med','big','timed'], so a 45-second Rush order is in EVERY shift, not only on a RUSH DAY. gemburrow/store/frames.json _forbidden_strings carries it with the note that it was caught on 08-21 and reintroduced on 08-22. index.html's 'No energy, no timers' card was the site's copy of the same defect and was replaced on 2026-08-24; the FAQ answer four sections down had been telling the truth about the 45-second dial the whole time.

SCOPE — the site never makes a page-level 'nothing leaves your device' claim, and it must not. index.html attaches the local claim to specific modes ('Career and Free digs send nothing') and gives the exception its own card ('One thing leaves your phone'), and privacy.html devotes a section to the Daily Dig post.
That mode split is real: the leaderboard submit at game.js:1776-1787 is inside an `if (this.isDaily)` branch, so a Career or Free run reaches no network code at all.
Progress itself is genuinely local: Meta.save() writes localStorage and the Capacitor Preferences mirror (game.js:684-689) and there is no sync path of ours anywhere in the client.
Career and Free digs make no network calls, so they are fully playable offline — same evidence as local_only (the isDaily branch at game.js:1776).

The Daily Dig is playable offline too, and the site says only that POSTING the score and drawing the board need a connection: an unsent score is kept in Meta.data.pendingScore (game.js:1780) and cleared only once a submission is acknowledged (game.js:1785), so it is retried on a later launch.

SCOPE (2026-08-14): this claim covers the iPHONE APP, where the music and art are files inside the app package (the audio/*.m4a fetch is same-origin to the WebView's bundle), so nothing about presentation needs the network. It does NOT cover the browser build at /gemburrow/play/, which ships no service worker and therefore fetches its assets over the network on first load. The site must not describe the browser build as playable offline.
